correctness.rationale: Exact identity at order one gives a nonincreasing positive product; invariant probabilities on compact nonsingular sets are supported on finitely many phase extrema, and the variational principle gives zero entropy. Away from order one the diagonal scalar map has either nonzero Chebyshev amplitude at zero, or (at order three) a nonzero linear amplitude. The reciprocal phase supplies arbitrarily many disjoint covering branches on shrinking intervals. On each branch the phase derivative dominates the smooth Chebyshev cross derivative in both Jacobian eigenvalues, yielding full N-symbol expanding repellers for every N and any fixed expansion margin. See RESULT.md Proof sections 1--4. Diagnostic code checks examples only.

value.rationale: The sharp order-one boundary is not a mere finite parameter estimate: it changes the compact recurrent entropy supremum from zero to infinity, identifies every invariant measure at the neutral order as a finite mixture of periodic measures, and establishes arbitrarily strong expansion in both ambient directions outside the neutral order. This is a structural warning about inferring exact compact recurrence from finite numerical Lyapunov indicators in a singular published map; the claim deliberately avoids unsupported physical-basin and cryptographic inferences.
